newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Stricken Venezuela tanker trans-shipment starts.
newsitem.headline: Stricken Venezuela tanker trans-shipment starts.

text.p: Crude oil remaining on the stricken oil tanker Nissos Amorgos was being pumped into another ship off the Venezuelan Caribbean coast on Monday afternoon, a shipping source said on Monday.
The Greek-flagged tanker ran aground on February 28 near the mouth of Venezuela's Lake Maracaibo, spilling about 25,000 barrels of its 476,000 barrel cargo.
The punctured hull was repaired last week and pumping into the new tanker Wilmington began at 1300 local time (1700 GMT) on Monday.
"The crisis seems to be over," the source said, predicting the pumping operation to be complete by midday Teusday. "It's going without any problems."
He said that latest tests showed the Nissos carrying 465,000 barrels of liquid, but the current cargo contained an unknown quantity of water.
Italian oil company Agip, a subsidiary of ENI and owners of the crude, planned to analyse the contents when all the crude was transferred onto the new tanker.

But attempts to refloat the Olympic Sponsor, another tanker which went aground on March 10 in exactly the same spot as the Nissos but without any spill, was still on hold waiting for an improvement in the weather.

A bunkering barge was at the scene ready to receive about 45,000 barrels of the 477,000 barrel cargo, but has been unable to begin pumping operations. "The weather has just been too rough to go alongside," a shipping source said.
He said they were hoping to get an opportunity to go ahead on Tuesday.

Shipping in the Lake Maracaibo channel has been restricted from 39.6 to 36 foot while the Olympic Sponsor stays aground, which shipping sources say should cut exports from the region by up to 150,000 barrels per day.
